argument_summary: The present record should not be read as support for clean certification. The supportable position is narrower: aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support release-level readiness, while the same admissible record also shows a named-use-case weakness in aviation maintenance triage and an incomplete draft runbook. On that evidence, the strongest defensible treatment is certification only with an explicit material caveat that the unresolved slice must be disclosed in launch documentation unless covered by approved risk acceptance. That narrows the actor claim to what the packet can actually support and avoids escalation beyond a bounded compliance caveat.
claims_about_business_cost: A bounded caveat is lower cost than escalation because it preserves the certification path while forcing the missing governance condition to be made explicit. Escalation is unnecessary if the auditor can treat this as a disclosure-gated compliance issue rather than a block created by aggregate readiness failure.
claims_about_policy: Policy does not support certification without material caveats here, because the record does not show either that no material weakness remains or that there is an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The policy does permit a narrower posture: if the unresolved aviation maintenance limitation is treated as a material limitation for the named launch use case, then the packet can be aligned with policy by requiring formal disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch. Draft monitoring materials can support risk management, but they do not remove the disclosure requirement on the current record.
concessions: The current record does not support clean certification without material caveats.
The draft runbook is incomplete under the stated policy because owner, alert threshold, and review-date evidence are missing.
The current record does not show approved risk acceptance.
The current record does not show that the limitation has already been formally disclosed in the model card or equivalent launch documentation.
